entries.2026-09-21: 2026-09-21 And we're off on the main class projects! We practiced a lot of things in the scrimmage. Meeting one another. Assessing strengths. Figuring out what we bring to the game. Now is not the time to just toss all that out and launch a new effort just like before. Apply what you practiced and learned. Yes. There needs to be a pizza in your team's future this week. Bootstrap fast. No project goes faster than the pace of the first week. Launch slow? Fail slow. Apply your principles, like ... survivability perhaps? Assess risk early and handle it head on. You should be taking active engineering control of the project, so ... what are we going to write down? What gaps need to be filled in, like, yesterday? Along the way we should prep a team charter. Plan on pushing one to your new team repo by late Friday. We'll talk more of what goes into this tomorrow but arrive to class with ideas about what you think needs to be clarified to get going. After all, you just practiced in the scrimmage. You should have some informed opinions now for what might have made things smoother. We already suggested some materials from LinkedInLearning. Now you might also take a look at characteristics of high-performing teams .

entries.2026-09-19: 2026-09-19 Scrimmage 3 grading summary is released. Saw a lot of good code blended with good intentions too. Plenty of great learning opportunities in this exercise! We will have much about which to talk, and even more to absorb and apply in the class projects coming up.
entries.2026-09-18: 2026-09-18 Scrimmages are in! Team reviews are in! Time for a weekend of reflection on what has been going on. Making decisions about what solves the problem is a whole different kettle of fish isn't it? Having someone else make those decisions so we can just go build them, and grind against known test data, sure simplifies the game a lot. Think about how your team made its decisions, what observations you made that informed the ways forward. What do you think we might make a specific point of doing differently in the class projects coming up? Software engineering is an exercise in what? Communication. And so far the most common challenge I have seen in scrimmage three has been gold plating the solution - making it harder to build, more elaborate to use. We are projecting way more of our own guesswork and biases into the decisions than we might. Which is to say, we didn't communicate as much as we might. Some teams did so in the last day or two. Good! Better late than not at all, but really -- waiting to find out something important after you build the app is a pretty expensive time to have that chat, wasn't it. Magically, our discussion topic for Tuesday is ... Discovery! Almost like we want you to dig deeper into properties of the class project early. Weekends are for reflection. Reflect!

entries.2026-09-03: 2026-09-03 A lab today using Gallup Strengths. Let's find what superhero powers we bring to help our teams win, and let's also use these powers to connect with one another. To assist in your weekend reflection please consider these supplemental materials. Quality improvement is an on-going game after all. LinkedIn Learning is a useful place to fish for fairly compact tutorials on software process and team practices. The material there by Chris Croft is a very nice starting point. And you can't beat the price. Theme Thursday is a resource I may have mentioned in class. Check it out after you've completed your Strengths reflections. This site features Gallup coaches working with project managers to tease out what the various strengths bring to the game.
entries.2026-09-02: 2026-09-02 Two new small exercises to get on your radar. You don't have enough details for how to do these now but you will by end of tomorrow's lab. First will be a one page submission of the Gallup Name it, Claim it, Aim it exercise. Details and examples in the lab, but after you do the practice tomorrow, do it again for real (when you have time to think about it) and submit it in your personal folder as "superhero.pdf" by SOB Tuesday, the 8th. At the same time, submit a one page 'infographic' to pitch yourself to others in the class. Again we will address this is more detail tomorrow but there is a lot of flex in what you offer. Submit this a PDF named for your directory ID. (If your campus directory ID is "morty" then the file will be "morty.pdf".) Do you notice the pattern here? We are giving a lot of weight to tasks which help us understand what we bring to the game, what strengths we use to bring success to a team, and how we are perceived by others. This is often pretty eye opening, and it gives better context for building solid relationships that are needed in a strong team. It works! (Let me know if any team wants to serve as the control group and use the "make shallow agreements, dial it in over discord, throw over the wall at end" processes. But my thought is: if you would like better project results than in the past then maybe you should try better processes than were used in the past...)
entries.2026-09-01: 2026-09-01 First class today. We went over some of the practice, made some introductions and got us all going on first assignments. To reproduce here a few points which came up along the way: "On time is late. Two minutes early is three minutes late." The grade server's zero-weight instruments ("phony baloney bonus points") are a way to offer insight on how other professionals might see your performance. We notice! So thanks to the several of you who completed the first assignment before class today - the early initiative got points. So did the intrepid adventurers who were first to engage in class with questions. Thanks! Looking forward to hearing the rest of you engage too! There are many ways we can interact, and commit messages on repository activity is another of them. These let me offer feedback and mentoring tips. If you're not tracking the messages we push from time to time then you aren't getting full value of the course. In steady state our work week will typically be a Tuesday discussion with some kind of lab activity on Thursdays. At start of semester we'll be a little out of cycle while we set a foundation; towards end of semester we'll err on the side of having more team time. Work week is for work . Pour it on. Weekends are for reflection . Let the lessons soak in. If you're not thinking about what happened then you're not learning in this class. Plan accordingly. Scrimmage assignments will be posted presently. Watch this space. Details count! Identify your textbook and support materials now, if you have not already. Bring your Gallup materials to Thursday lab!

The initial assignments are due Thursday as detailed in the 2026-08-08 post below. We'll see you in class Tuesday. We have many small tasks to field right now, and with fast pace. entries.2026-08-08: 2026-08-08 A new semester is just around the corner. We're sharing the the first assignments for those who want to get an early start. Review our guide on Expectations Management! Please make sure we are all clear about what we're getting into by reviewing the guide Is 435 right for me? Get started on the first assignments! Getting these very small tasks out of the way will keep the decks cleared for more interesting things once the semester arrives. Purchase your Clifton Strengths assessment. This skills assessment is for our exercises on team building and is available for a student discounted rate from the folks at Gallup: Clifton Strengths for Students (The "Top 5" report is adequate for our needs, but the student version offers those and more at the same price.) Save and study the PDF reports, which are specific to each person; we'll have you place the Signature Themes Report in your Subversion folder (which you will receive first day of semester.) We will use this material in our first lab, so don't be left out. Update your resume. Prepare this as a PDF document. Please only share details with which you are comfortable. We use the content later in sorting out talents for teams and projects, and to figure out early who knows how to follow directions (which is one of the most basic skill sets of our business.) Place this in a PDF document "resume.pdf" in your repository folder as well. Prepare a thoughtful statement of what you want to get out of 435. Craft this as a Word document, and place it in your Subversion folder as file "goals.docx".   In general we judge more than just the payload of your submissions, so please remember that evidence of timeliness, preparation and planning always count. Everything you do reflects on you . Students on the waitlist should plan to attend the class from day one and perform the above assignments in anticipation of being admitted to the section. We will issue repository credentials to waitlisted students so you are able to participate in the labs and complete the exercises for on-time credit once you are able to add the class. Let's emphasize this: you must participate and do the work from day one in order to get the credit. Pro tip: Commit to success from day one. We rely on workmanship offered in early assignments when making decisions on teaming and tasking, so consider seriously what we will have to work with. Overall, exercise of initiative in the interest of quality is rewarded , so pay attention, demonstrate decent critical thinking skills and focus on success from the start. Do that and we'll make the semester worth your while. Assignments On the first day of the semester we will email credentials for access to the class repository (which is one of several ways we will communicate this semester) to each student registered. Our first assignments (as above) will be due by SOB on Thursday, September 3rd. Infographic Plan on prepping a simple infographic on yourself to pitch for team members (even if already on a team) for early the following week. You'll have plenty of ideas for how to do this based on our first lab, using resume and Gallup Strengths. Teams We will form four-person teams starting the first day of class. These teams will conduct practice exercises ("scrimmages") early in semester in order to get used to some of the basics before we tackle the class project. You're free to form these teams as you like, though don't panic if you don't know anyone else in class since we'll make time available adjacent to each class in order to meet one another.
entries.2026-09-30: 2026-09-30 Plan hard, build easy. Plan hard build easy. Say it with me again: plan hard, build easy. All of which means we are exercising discipline to have hard conversations about functionality, platforms, test plans and more now rather than defer them to the point of delivery, when, in reality, there is no ability to do anything about any disagreements or surprises. It sure is easy to duck hard questions about how to resolve ambiguities. It is easy to ignore the stuff we're teaching, groove on the positive waves of good intentions and proceed like this is some generic programming exercise in a prior class. This lasts up until we have a head on collision with reality once a client tries to use our product. That's the point when all the gaps we covered up start to stick out badly. All at once. Honest: it is a lot less uncomfortable to hammer issues out today than in December. Do your future self a favor and humor me by trying out these active discovery techniques to surface hard issues now. Learn the professional practices by trying them (and seeing a positive outcome) instead of ignoring them (and learning what you should have done.)
entries.2026-09-29: 2026-09-29 More discussion today about notations available for us to model systems under study. The language we choose nuances what we can express about it, which is why we choose models carefully and with intention to span perspectives.
entries.2026-09-27: 2026-09-27 A busy new week begins. As mentioned in last Thursday's lab, I have opened a team engagement poll on the mentors site. Please take a moment to complete this right away. I will harvest it over coffee early Wednesday, so whatever constitutes "end of day" for you on Tuesday is the effective deadline. Also per lab discussion, let's plan on having each team prepare both a detailed Amazon Press Release and a planning document answering questions according to the Heilmeier Catechism . These should be word documents in project repo ("amazon.docx" and "heilmeier.docx" respectively). For best effect, I suggest not worring about this immediately. First focus on a kick-ass pitch for our visitors on Thursday, factor in their suggestions, feedback and advice, and then bake that new insight into these planning documents. Remember, we are practicing use of our Principles of SE too, so we will check how well the growing base of materials line up. Shoot for having this in sometime NLT "over the weekend" meaning I will check them out over first coffee Monday morning.
entries.2026-09-25: 2026-09-25 We launch this week with mixed effort but with most teams having enjoyed a substantive exchange with the clients. This gets us something to research as we flesh out design options in prep for pitching to our experts (alumni) on Thursday. Our alumni are ready to give deep insights on ways forward; give them deeply researched designs for consideration. This weekend, take some time to reflect on all that needs to go into the full spec for approval (the so-called "green light to build.") It's a lot. And it all needs to line up. Remember that principle? "We get confidence in the quality of software by expressing it in multiple, independent ways that can be checked." The spec asks us to express the solution in terms of functionality, cost, test results and much more. We don't want a bag of mixed puzzle pieces that don't look related to one another; we'd love to see a cohesive story colored in about the solution, and supported with piloting. What can we run soon to reduce risk of failure? There are plenty of options. Yes ... there is much on which to reflect this weekend.

entries.2026-10-05: 2026-10-05 Did you find focusing value from those Amazon and Heilmeier exercises? Some common issues flagged ... The Heilmeier docs were generally too wordy. Learn to say something specific and short . Cost estimates were mostly bogus (as we expected ...) Teams often stated what they were willing to spend (hours to invest) and not the time needed to actually build that product. We don't care what you want to spend. We don't care what you are willing to spend. We want to know what the job actually takes. That's a lot harder to come up with, isn't it.
entries.2026-10-06: 2026-10-06 We slightly adjusted the agenda for this week to push requirements expression to Thursday, with lab today. We discussed cost estimation and validation, at least to the level as we will need for use in crafting our green lights. Again, why look at our products in so many ways? We are intentionally creating new perspectives for viewing the space in order to check whether they all line up. This is valid application of one of our principles. When we have opportunity to talk and reason about our software without yet building the software, it turns out we learn a lot about it. We are more likely to build the right thing in the first place. How are those superhero powers working out? Are you using them? Do they work? Reflect on this in a ticket this week so we can track the successes. While you're at it, take a moment to reflect on your original goals statement in the class. How is that coming along? Feel free to update it (not replace it) to make the objectives more testable, and maybe annotate them with this mid point assessment of how we are reaching them.
